rationale: The startup-replay account states a quantitative boundary: the replay can enqueue at most 128 batches, so the entry limit is 128 times MaxAppendEntries. Two configurations have supported that product so far, 64 entries per batch (8192 entries) and 1024 (131072 entries). This experiment adds the smallest legal batch size, 1, where the predicted boundary is only 128 entries. Exact controls on both sides of that boundary test the product directly: 128 entries at one entry per batch is exactly 128 batches and should return, 129 entries is 129 batches and should not. A local probe matched the prediction, with the control returning in under a millisecond and the 129-entry case never returning while one goroutine sat in processLogs and nothing was applied. The formal run is requested so the third configuration point rests on a retained receipt.

scope.description: One node with RestoreCommittedLogs enabled and MaxAppendEntries set to 1, started from an in-memory commit-tracking log store seeded with either exactly 128 command entries or 129, with the staged commit index equal to the seeded entry count and no snapshot. The harness calls NewRaft on a separate goroutine and bounds the wait, because a caller that observes no return cannot call Shutdown: NewRaft has not handed back the *Raft. It records whether the constructor returned, how long it took, the error, how many entries the FSM had applied when the observation ended, and whether a new goroutine was left inside processLogs.
assumptions: The seeded entries are ordinary command entries at term 1, which restoreFromCommittedLogs replays without needing a configuration entry.
One second of observation is ample for a replay of 128 entries: the control case returns in about a millisecond on the same machine.
A constructor that has not returned within the observation window is treated as having made no progress, which is what the harness measures rather than assumes.
excluded: No real cluster, no snapshot and no configuration entry in the replayed range.
Only MaxAppendEntries=1; the batch sizes 64 and 1024 were measured by earlier receipts.
No attempt to shut down a node whose constructor never returned.

experiment.prefix: The harness seeds an InmemCommitTrackingStore with N command entries at term 1, stages the commit index to N, and starts one raft with RestoreCommittedLogs enabled and MaxAppendEntries=1, whose local id is node1 and whose timeouts are 50 ms. It emits rb_case_<case> with the mode, the flag, the entries, the staged commit index, the last log index, the replay entry and batch counts and the observation timeout, then calls NewRaft on a goroutine and waits up to the timeout. On return it shuts the node down; on timeout it records that no return was observed and leaves the node alone, since the *Raft was never handed back. It emits rb_result_<case> with returned, elapsed_ms, error, the FSM's applied count sampled after the observation, and the change in the number of goroutines whose stack contains processLogs. The control case seeds 128 entries and allows ten seconds; the trigger seeds 129 entries and allows five.
semantic_changes: MaxAppendEntries is set to 1 rather than the default 64 or the previously exercised 1024, so the replay needs one batch per entry.
The seeded log sizes are 128 and 129 entries instead of 8192 and 8193, which keeps the control cheap enough to run beside the trigger.
The events keep the same field names as the earlier startup harness so the three configuration points can be compared directly.
experiment.responsibility: Starting a node from already-committed entries is a startup path the library offers, and it must either complete or report an error. A constructor that blocks because it produced into a channel whose only consumer it has not started yet cannot do either: the caller never receives the node, so the caller has no way to start, serve or shut it down. The experiment measures the exact entry count at which that happens at the smallest legal batch size, which tests the stated product rather than a single configuration.

comparisons.description: Exactly 128 batches, one entry each, is within the channel capacity and must let the constructor return.
One entry past the boundary must still let the constructor return; the harness records that it does not.
A completed replay would leave all 129 replayed entries applied to the state machine.
